readback.name: Poincare.DeTurckTensorBasis.tensor_expansion
readback.mathematical_statement: E is the fixed real three-dimensional Euclidean space ClosedSmoothModel 3, e_a=basis3 a is its standard Euclidean basis, Bilin is E ->L[R] E ->L[R] R, and Jet1 is E ->L[R] Bilin. The pinned coordinate q_a = coordinate a is the actual continuous real coordinate functional of this Euclidean basis, built by converting its linear coordinate map to a CLM. The pinned tensor a b is q_a.smulRight q_b, so tensor_ab(v,w)=q_a(v)*q_b(w). The pinned firstJet p a b is q_p.smulRight(tensor a b), so firstJet_pab(r,v,w)=q_p(r)*(q_a(v)*q_b(w)). These scalar actions are ordinary real scalar multiplication on the original CLM spaces, not matrix multiplication. All index ranges below are Fin 3 and all declarations have no universe parameters. For every arbitrary h in Bilin, h equals the double finite sum over every ordered pair a,b of h(e_a)(e_b) smul tensor a b. This is equality of the whole continuous-bilinear-map object, hence reconstruction in all vector slots, not just equality at one basis evaluation. It retains nine ordered component slots. No symmetry assumption identifies the distinct a,b and b,a slots, and no half-off-diagonal or factor-two convention is introduced. There is no positive-definiteness, invertibility, metric-realization, manifold, chart, time, Hoelder exponent, background datum, coefficient map, norm estimate, or supplied package premise. The statement is this explicit reconstruction formula; it does not itself bundle a Basis object or assert a separate orthogonality or norm identity, construct a Graph operator, or establish a flow or global L.

readback.name: Poincare.DeTurckTensorBasis.firstJet_expansion
readback.mathematical_statement: E is the fixed real three-dimensional Euclidean space ClosedSmoothModel 3, e_a=basis3 a is its standard Euclidean basis, Bilin is E ->L[R] E ->L[R] R, and Jet1 is E ->L[R] Bilin. The pinned coordinate q_a = coordinate a is the actual continuous real coordinate functional of this Euclidean basis, built by converting its linear coordinate map to a CLM. The pinned tensor a b is q_a.smulRight q_b, so tensor_ab(v,w)=q_a(v)*q_b(w). The pinned firstJet p a b is q_p.smulRight(tensor a b), so firstJet_pab(r,v,w)=q_p(r)*(q_a(v)*q_b(w)). These scalar actions are ordinary real scalar multiplication on the original CLM spaces, not matrix multiplication. All index ranges below are Fin 3 and all declarations have no universe parameters. For every arbitrary J in Jet1, J equals the triple finite sum over every ordered p,a,b of J(e_p)(e_a)(e_b) smul firstJet p a b. The first index p is the first-jet direction slot and the indices a,b are the bilinear tensor slots. This is equality of the whole CLM-valued first jet, with all 27 ordered components retained. J need not be the derivative of a realized field and need not have symmetry in any slots. The declaration locally selects the canonical Mathlib CLM normed additive group and real normed-space structures for Jet1, with real source and target scalars, source E, target Bilin, and RingHom.id R. The accompanying canonical background-space and Prod additive-monoid caches add no data premise and change no norm or operation. In particular the original Jet1 operator norm and real scalar action are retained. No manifold, chart, time, Hoelder exponent, metric value, invertibility, coefficient bound, or actual-flow package is assumed. The statement is the explicit first-jet reconstruction, and does not by itself produce a derivative certificate, quantitative norm estimate, Graph carrier construction, or global L.

readback.name: Poincare.DeTurckTensorBasis.coefficient_action
readback.mathematical_statement: E is the fixed real three-dimensional Euclidean space ClosedSmoothModel 3, e_a=basis3 a is its standard Euclidean basis, Bilin is E ->L[R] E ->L[R] R, and Jet1 is E ->L[R] Bilin. The pinned coordinate q_a = coordinate a is the actual continuous real coordinate functional of this Euclidean basis, built by converting its linear coordinate map to a CLM. The pinned tensor a b is q_a.smulRight q_b, so tensor_ab(v,w)=q_a(v)*q_b(w). The pinned firstJet p a b is q_p.smulRight(tensor a b), so firstJet_pab(r,v,w)=q_p(r)*(q_a(v)*q_b(w)). These scalar actions are ordinary real scalar multiplication on the original CLM spaces, not matrix multiplication. All index ranges below are Fin 3 and all declarations have no universe parameters. Let L0 : Bilin ->L[R] Bilin and L1 : Jet1 ->L[R] Bilin be any continuous real-linear maps, let h in Bilin and J in Jet1 be arbitrary independent inputs, and let c,d be any output indices. The pinned entryCLM c d evaluates a Bilin first at e_c and then at e_d. The theorem asserts both of the following separate equations for these same data. First, entryCLM c d (L0 h) equals the double sum over a,b of entryCLM c d (L0(tensor a b)) * h(e_a)(e_b). Second, entryCLM c d (L1 J) equals the triple sum over p,a,b of entryCLM c d (L1(firstJet p a b)) * J(e_p)(e_a)(e_b). Thus c,d label the output tensor slots, a,b label input tensor slots, and p labels the input first-jet direction. The scalar coefficient arrays are actual evaluations of L0/L1 on the pinned elementary tensors and first jets; no arbitrary coefficient arrays or extra coefficient package are supplied in their place. All products and finite sums in these scalar equations are ordinary real arithmetic. There is no transpose, slot swap, symmetric-six reduction, or identification of J with a derivative of h. The conclusion is a conjunction of the two separate action formulas, not a third formula for L0 h + L1 J. The maps L0 and L1 are arbitrary CLMs rather than necessarily the actual g0 zeroOrder/firstOrder maps, so applying this algebra to those maps is a subsequent use of the theorem. The canonical Jet1/CLM real group and normed-space preamble and the standard Prod additive-monoid cache preserve the original norms, scalar actions, addition and zero; no new norm, supplied instance, or quantitative bound is introduced. No symmetry, realized metric/jet field, invertibility, manifold, chart, time, Hoelder exponent, smooth spatial coefficient, Graph norm, or flow premise occurs. The theorem provides the scalar component action of these existing linear maps only; it does not construct the actual spatial coefficient fields, smooth compact buffers, coupled Graph forcing operator, tensor covariance, bounded global L, or signed residual/contraction.
